t.2.83.1: Having spent the night right there on the bank of the Gaṅgā, that Rāghava, Bharata, rose at dawn and spoke these words to Śatrughna.
t.2.83.2: Śatrughna, rise up! Why do you lie there? Quickly bring Guha, lord of the Niṣādas; may good fortune be with you. He will carry the army across.
t.2.83.3: Prompted by his brother, Śatrughna too spoke thus: “I am awake, I do not sleep, for I too am thinking of the noble one.”
t.2.83.4: While those two lions among men were thus conversing with one another, Guha came at the right time with joined palms and spoke to Bharata.
t.2.83.5: Did you spend the night pleasantly on the riverbank, O Kākutstha? And is all well with you and with your army?
t.2.83.6: Having heard those words of Guha, spoken out of affection, Bharata, devoted to Rāma, in turn spoke these words.
t.2.83.7: Pleasant was our night, O king, and we have been honored by you as well. Now let the fishermen ferry us across the Gaṅgā with many boats.
t.2.83.8: Then Guha, having heard Bharata's command, hastened back into the town and spoke to that assembly of his kinsmen.
t.2.83.9: Rise up, awake! May good fortune be with you always. Haul the boats together, and we shall ferry the army across.
t.2.83.10: Thus addressed, they rose up and, hastening at the command of the prince, gathered from every side five hundred boats.
t.2.83.11: Other boats, excellent ones, could be recognized by their svastika marks; they bore great bells, gleamed with fluttering flags, caught the wind well and were sturdily built.
t.2.83.12: Then Guha brought up a splendid boat, marked with the auspicious svastika, covered with pale woolen blankets, and resounding with joyful acclaim.
t.2.83.13: Bharata boarded it, and mighty Śatrughna too, and Kausalyā and Sumitrā, and whatever other royal women there were.
t.2.83.14: The family priest went at the front, together with the elders and the brāhmaṇas; right after them came the king's wives, and likewise the carts and the market stalls.
t.2.83.16: Then those swift boats, adorned with banners and steered by the fishermen themselves, sped onward, carrying the people who had boarded them.
t.2.83.15: The uproar of those setting fire to their encampment, plunging into the ford, and gathering up their goods touched the very heavens.
t.2.83.17: Some of the boats were filled with women, some with horses, and some there carried carriages and draught animals of great value.
t.2.83.18: The boats went to the far shore, set those people down, and turned back, while the fishermen's kinsmen performed many varied feats of boatmanship on the water.
t.2.83.19: The elephants bearing victory banners, urged on by their riders, shone as they crossed the river, like mountains crowned with flags.
t.2.83.20: Some climbed aboard the boats, while others crossed on rafts; some crossed with the help of pots and jars, and others crossed by swimming with their arms.
t.2.83.22: Having reassured the army and settled it at ease as it pleased, the great-souled Bharata, surrounded by his priests, set out to see Bharadvāja, foremost among the seers.
t.2.83.21: That auspicious army, ferried across the Gaṅgā by the fishermen themselves, set out at the hour called Maitra for the excellent forest of Prayāga.
